messages:
olivia_csm: Quick weekly sync for Asterwell — focused on token usage + throughput (WoW / QoQ). Posting the short summary and flags :wave:

maria_cs: Thanks! dropping the numbers I pulled this morning.

maria_cs: WoW tokens: +18% (1.2M -> 1.42M). QoQ tokens: +68%.
maria_cs: Avg throughput sustained: baseline 120 rps -> 190 rps peak during daytime window.
maria_cs: 95p latency: 220ms -> 275ms WoW spike.
maria_cs: Error rate (5xx): 0.4% -> 1.3% (largest on /chat generate route).
maria_cs: Spend WoW: +22% (driven by longer responses and more retries).

raj_engineer: thx. any correlation with model switch or batch config?

maria_cs: they moved to quantized-mix-v2 on Tuesday for cost tests; that's when the uptick starts. Also they enabled longer default max_tokens in the client.

raj_engineer: ok — quantized-mix-v2 can increase CPU on host for certain seq lengths; curious if batching policy changed. can @tim_ops pull runtime config?

tim_ops: pulling traces now. infra-bot: start fetch traces for Asterwell from 2462030000..2462109000

infra-bot: trace job 98321 queued. ETA ~2m.

tim_ops: quick grep of deploy logs — there was a canary on quantized-mix-v2 at 2024-11-12 09:18 UTC (customer opt-in). Client default increased max_tokens from 256->512 on 2024-11-13 03:06 UTC.

olivia_csm: so combination of model variant + longer responses explains tokens and spend. The latency + error spike likely from runtime pressure during peak.

raj_engineer: agree. propose short remediation plan: 1) temporarily cap client max_tokens at 384 for Asterwell via per-customer config; 2) revert to quantized-mix-v1 for canary subset if errors persist; 3) adjust batching window to smaller size for their peak region.

olivia_csm: can we estimate impact if we cap max_tokens to 384? maria, you want to run a quick sim?

maria_cs: running quick ballpark: if avg response length drops from 420 -> 340 tokens, expected WoW token delta ~ -16% and spend would drop ~ -12%. Latency 95p might come down ~30-40ms.

raj_engineer: good. tim, can you implement per-customer cap and a short canary revert?

tim_ops: yes. I'll push a flow control override for Asterwell to limit max_tokens=384 and route 10% of traffic to quantized-mix-v1 canary. Will monitor for 1 hour, rollback if regressions.

olivia_csm: schedule: tim to deploy at 12:15 UTC, monitor for 60m; marIa to post updated telemetry at 13:30 UTC.

maria_cs: ack. I'll post a delta snapshot after the hour.

olivia_csm: action items:
- tim_ops: deploy per-customer cap + canary (12:15 UTC).
- maria_cs: telemetry snapshot (13:30 UTC).
- raj_engineer: look into kernel scheduling impact of quantized-mix-v2 for long sequences.
- olivia_csm: prep enablement note for Asterwell (explaining cap + invite to enablement call).

maria_cs: quick reference query I ran:
```sql
SELECT date, SUM(tokens) as tokens, p95_latency_ms
FROM customer_metrics
WHERE customer_id='asterwell'
AND date >= '2024-10-01'
GROUP BY date
ORDER BY date DESC
LIMIT 14;
```

olivia_csm: flagged renewal risk low currently but call recommended to explain temporary cap and cost optimization. I'll book a 30m touchpoint for tomorrow.

tim_ops: infra-bot status: traces complete, CPU-kernel queue showed backpressure aligned with 95p latency spikes.

raj_engineer: noted. likely queuing in attention kernels for long sequences. I'll prototype a quick micro-bench on quantized-mix-v2 with 512 seq to validate.

olivia_csm: thanks team. will update Asterwell and post follow-up here after telemetry. :thumbsup:

maria_cs: update (13:34 UTC): after cap + canary — tokens WoW reduced ~14% vs pre-change, 95p latency down ~45ms, 5xx down to 0.5%. Spend trending down. Posting charts to the CS dashboard.

olivia_csm: perfect. I'll send the enablement note + invite now.

tim_ops: leaving watch on their pool for next 24h. ping me if anything spikes.

olivia_csm: closing thread for now — will reopen if anomalies reappear. Thanks everyone!
